title: relay_queue write-order is load-bearing and correctly documented
description: relay_queue::enqueue writes .msg first, then .env. The comment correctly explains why: if .env existed without .msg the drain would attempt to read a non-existent payload. The drain only iterates .env files and reads the paired .msg, so the write order ensures a partial crash leaves no dangling .env. This is a deliberate crash-safety decision. The comment is accurate for the actual .env-first scan pattern and should be preserved. (Note: the orphan-.msg issue is a separate problem — the comment is correct about the .env-first concern, just incomplete about the .msg-without-.env case.)
